title: Ernie Andrews's first record, "Soothe Me," and the flat fifty-dollar fee
summary: Callender supplied the bridge to Joe Green's hit; he and Willard agree that the flat fee for Andrews's later hit was exploitation.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: And that brings to mind another 17-year-old, Ernie Andrews. I did his first record date, a thing called "Soothe Me."
Oh, I remember that. Was that for Gene Norman?

That was on a label called Gem, I think. No, it wasn't Gene Norman. Joe Green had a lot to do with it. Because Joe wrote the tune, "Soothe Me," and I supplied the bridge. I didn't get any credit for it, but anyhow, the bridge to "Soothe Me" was by Red Callender.
Oh, that was something of a hit.
It was a big hit. Stan Kenton later recorded it.
I have Ernie's recording of that. He had another hit for Gene that I think he said he got made $50 for, "Make Me..."
Oh, yeah. That's an Eddie Beal-Joe Green tune. Well, Gene never did throw his money around, and fifty dollars wasn't too bad in those days...
...if you got artist royalties to go with it.
But no, he didn't. Ernie said he got a flat fifty for that record.
Well, that was exploitation, wasn't it.
That was exploitation. It's nice to have a hit, but...
